title: Adaptive slot plan and tenant cost prescriptions
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: produce tenant-specific, SLA-aware 'slot prescriptions' that recommend conserved or expanded dedicated capacity with an estimated monthly cost delta, recommended autoscale profiles, and a confidence score. The feature should combine utilization telemetry, throughput SLO targets, model mix signals, and simulated workload replays to create actionable recommendations surfaced in Console and via an API for automation.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine runs daily and produces a ranked list of actions per tenant (grow/shrink/hold) with estimated monthly EUR/USD savings or cost increase and a confidence score

Recommendations respect tenant-level SLAs: any shrink action must include headroom and a safe rollback policy; predicted request success rate degradation < 0.5% for P99 latency target breaches in simulation
Simulator uses last 30 days of real traffic, supports burst windows, and reproduces observed 95th percentile token throughput within 10% error compared to historical metrics
Console UI shows top-5 recommended actions with one-click apply (creates a proposal PR to provisioning service) and a preview modal with simulated SLO traces
API endpoint (/v1/dedicated/recommendations) returns JSON payload with actions, reason, savings_estimate_usd, confidence in schema validated by e2e tests
Canary rollout: feature enabled for 5% of tenants first, with automatic rollback if error budget burn increases by >10% vs baseline
Automated tests (unit + integration) covering simulation engine, ranking logic, and permission gates are added to CI
Documentation includes a playbook describing operational guardrails, how to interpret confidence, and an incident checklist
tasks: Data: extend telemetry pipeline to emit per-tenant slot utilization, model-mix histograms, burst windows (ENG-217304 dependency)
Modeling: build simulation harness that replays token-level traces against candidate slot counts and autoscale configs
Policy: define shrink/grow rules that encode SLA thresholds, minimum reserve, and tenant tiering (free/dev/prod)
Backend: implement recommendation service, daily batch job, and API surface
Console: design and implement recommendations view, preview modal, and one-click apply flow
Infra: add feature flag, canary rollout controls, and rate limits for API consumers
E2E: integration tests that validate recommendations do not increase P99 latency for canary tenants
Docs/SE: write customer-facing playbook and run internal training for Solutions Eng
updates: 2025-02-18: Initial spike complete — analyzed 60 tenants across 3 months. Observed steady-state slot utilization ranges 28-72%; tail bursts are main driver of conservative commits.
2025-02-24: Prototype simulator notebook committed (github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/pull/44). Basic replay matches historical throughput within 12% for 80% of tenants.

2025-02-28: Design review with PM and Console (notes in Confluence: /spaces/DEDICATED/pages/Adaptive+Slot+Plan). PM requested per-tenant confidence breakdown and an ‘explain’ field for each recommendation.
2025-03-02: Telemetry work blocked by missing burst window metric — dependency ticket ENG-50321 prioritized; Diego paired with SRE to unblock.
2025-03-04: Prototype ranking adjusted to penalize recommendations that require >20% change in committed slots in a single action; UX mockups approved pending API schema updates
risks: Underestimating burst tail patterns could cause increased 429s or latency regressions if shrink actions applied too aggressively
Telemetry gaps (missing per-tenant burst histograms) will reduce recommendation confidence and delay rollout
Customers on contractual reserved capacity may object to automated shrink suggestions; we must surface billing implications clearly
Simulator complexity — overfitting to past traffic may miss new traffic modes after client changes
notes: Trade-offs discussed: conservative defaults vs aggressive savings. We settled on conservative shrink thresholds for prod tenants and more permissive suggestions for dev/test. We will provide an opt-in 'aggressive mode' for customers who want maximal cost savings and accept higher SLO risk.
implementation_strategy: Phase 1: daily recommendations + console UI read-only. Phase 2: add one-click apply that creates provisioning proposals. Phase 3: automated apply for low-tier dev tenants behind aggressive flag.
observability_plan: Expose metric dedicated.recommendations.applied, dedicated.recommendations.previewed, and a canary.error_budget_burn dashboard. Add alerts if canary error budget burn > 10% relative baseline for 1h.
owner_notes: Diego to sync with SRE on telemetry SLOs next week. Aim to have a minimal viable recommendation pipeline and Console surface by mid-April. Coordinate release with Billing for messaging to customers.
